title: SDK public sample apps and thematic templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose:
This page consolidates a curated set of small, production-oriented sample applications and thematic template bundles for Redwood SDK integrations. The artifacts are intended to be used as: quickstarts for new teams, reference implementations for common product patterns, and contribution targets for new SDK features.

Audience:
- SDK engineers, integration engineers, and solutions engineers who need runnable examples they can fork and extend.
- Developer advocates creating tutorial material.
- Customer engineers validating an integration pattern.

Summary of bundles included:
| bundle | intent | language(s) | runtime style | key Redwood features shown |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| support-chat-v2 | Customer-facing chat with tools and database lookups | python, node | serverless-friendly | streaming, tool-calls, rate-limit handling |
| embeddings-search-demo | Multi-doc semantic search + reranking | python | long-running service | embeddings, caching, query routing |
| doc-ingest-pipeline | Document ingestion + chunking + vector store | node | batch + worker | batching, KV cache warmup, quantization notes |
| edge-proxy-adapter | Local edge adapter for offline fallback | go, node | sidecar | local fallback, telemetry hooks |
| modal-llm-playground | Fine-grained prompt templates + evaluation harness | python | dev-only | templating, evals, prompt set integration |

Location and repo links (internal):
- Primary monorepo: git@internal:redwood/sdk-sample-bundles (canonical master)
- Short-lived forks for demos: git@internal:redwood/dx-demo-<bundle>

Quickstart — clone and run (common steps)
1) Clone the canonical monorepo and change into the example directory:
   git clone git@internal:redwood/sdk-sample-bundles.git
   cd sdk-sample-bundles/bundles/support-chat-v2
2) Create a .env (example below) and export locally: see .env.example
3) Install dependencies and run the dev server (example shown for Python):
   python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxxx
   export REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood-inference.internal
   ./dev_server.sh

Example .env.example (do not commit secrets)
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-<REDACTED>
REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood-inference.internal
REDWOOD_PROJECT=demo-support-chat
LOG_LEVEL=debug
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otel-ingest.internal:4317

API usage snippets (Python)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), base_url=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_URL'))
# streaming example for chat output
with client.chat_stream(model="rwd-small-1", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Help me find invoice 4823"}]) as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='')

Adapter example (Node) — local sidecar pattern
// HTTP adapter that translates app payload to Redwood API calls
const express = require('express')
const app = express()
app.post('/local-chat', async (req, res) => {
  // translate and forward to Redwood through local credentials or direct fallback
})

Telemetry and observability guidance
- Each sample includes an OpenTelemetry scaffold. Configure OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT in .env for dev/staging.
- Recommended spans: request.receive, redwood.call, redwood.stream, downstream.db.lookup.
- Attach these tags to all Redwood client calls: service.redwood.bundle, bundle.version, env.
- Suggested error rate alert during demo runs: >1% 5m window (reduce noisy alerts by excluding synthetic test tokens).

SLOs and performance notes for sample apps
- Demo latency targets (for dev/staging): P50 < 120ms for non-streaming embed calls; P95 < 600ms for chat with streaming off.
- Cost guidance: use quantized model variants in demos for cost-limited environments; see quantization_guidelines.md in repo.

Canonical fixes and common support patterns included in the bundles
- Retry with idempotency token pattern: examples include retry middleware for transient 5xx and 429 with exponential backoff.
- Circuit breaker wrapper: demonstrates graceful fallback to secondary model or cached response after N consecutive failures.
- Telemetry mismatch debugging: sample script that replays a failing trace and compares token-level timing to local simulated server.

Contribution and release process for the sample bundles
1) Branch off 'main' with prefix bundle/<bundle-name>/feature
2) Implement code and add a smoke test script under ./smoke-tests/<bundle>
3) Update the bundle manifest file bundles/manifest.yml with new version and changelog line
4) Open a PR, assign reviewers listed in this doc, and attach a short GIF demonstrating the app running
5) CI will run linters, unit tests, and a containerized smoke test. After merge, the package is tagged as: bundle-<bundle>-vX.Y.Z and published to our internal artifact index.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-dx (SDK examples) — eng-dx@redwood.internal
- Maintainer for support-chat-v2: Marcus Hill (marcus.hill@redwood.internal)
- Maintainer for embeddings-search-demo: Lina Chen (lina.chen@redwood.internal)

Onboarding notes for non-engineers
- Solutions engineers: there is a workspace with pre-provisioned API keys and a step-by-step slide deck in the /sales folder of the repo. Follow the "Slides -> Run demo" section.
- Developer advocates: use modal-llm-playground for tutorial videos — it includes a built-in recording toggle and synthetic data mode.

Operational runbook snippets (for demos in staging)
- If a demo experiences persistent 503s:
  1. Check REDWOOD_API_URL and DNS resolution
  2. Confirm API key validity: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" $REDWOOD_API_URL/v1/health
  3. Inspect application logs and traces in the OTEL backend for redwood.call errors
  4. If rate-limited, rotate to the low-traffic demo key and add a note to the bundle's README

FAQs
Q: Can I use these bundles with the Hosted offering?
A: Yes — update REDWOOD_API_URL to the hosted endpoint and set a hosted API key. Some demo configurations assume lower quotas; change model to a hosted-compatible SKU.

Q: Are the bundles production-ready?
A: They are reference-quality prototypes intentionally configured for clarity and educational value, not hardened production services. Use the design notes in each bundle (design.md) before productionizing.

---
# bundles/manifest.yml
bundles:
  - name: support-chat-v2
    version: 0.7.0
    path: bundles/support-chat-v2
    owner: marcus.hill@redwood.internal
    quickstart: true
    smoke_test: ./smoke-tests/support-chat.sh
  - name: embeddings-search-demo
    version: 0.5.2
    path: bundles/embeddings-search-demo
    owner: lina.chen@redwood.internal
    quickstart: true
---

Please follow the contribution checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md and include a recorded demo for all new bundles.
